agree.reason: The pacing argument (13 members a week needed against 35 a week reached) and the June checkpoint give sceptical board members something solid to weigh, but the misread ad trend makes the first-year gap look larger than it is, and the empty placeholders on the bridge funding and the 11-year colleague's role leave the two sales-minded members room to hold back.

honest.reason: The memo turns the requested 'will replace' into a stated goal and does not invent figures, but it says the 36% fall happened 'over two years' when it happened in one.

works_the_facts.reason: The derivations are correct and useful: 1.5% sign-up, about $20k a year, 875 members, 6.25% of the list, 13 against 35 a week and about $52k in year one. The do-nothing projection uses about 20% a year instead of 36%, so it gives roughly $67k where it should give about $54k.

right_comparison.reason: Because the decline is treated as spread over two years, ads look about $13k healthier in 2027 than the trend suggests, and that turns a near-even first year ($52k against about $54k) into an apparent $15k shortfall.

qualification.reason: The 500-members-by-June-30 trigger, with options brought to the board and monthly reporting on members and cancellations, is a dated, numeric and checkable condition with a stated consequence.

objections.reason: The memo meets the likely objections about a loyal early cohort, unknown churn and the fallback to sponsorships or ads, but the colleague's future is left as a placeholder, and the overstated gap raises a funding worry that the real trend would largely answer.

fit.reason: It is a clearly sectioned memo of about one page, though several unfilled placeholders mean it isn't ready to send.
